guarantees.claim: For each i in [0, NumAlerts-1], a prim_alert_sender is instantiated with .AsyncOn=AlertAsyncOn[i] and .IsFatal=AlertIsFatal[i], driving alert_tx_o[i].
All prim_alert_sender instances have their .alert_req_i input connected to the single-bit signal alerts[0].
The .alert_ack_o and .alert_state_o outputs of each prim_alert_sender instance are left unconnected.

assumptions.claim: External logic must drive alerts[0] as the combined alert request for all alert instances, because only bit 0 is connected.
assumptions.risk: If external logic drives alert requests on other bits of alerts, those requests are ignored, and the corresponding alert senders will not be triggered.

uncertain_points.claim: All alert_req_i ports are connected to alerts[0]; it is unclear whether alerts is intended to be a multi-bit bus with per-alert requests (likely alerts[i]) or correctly uses a single shared request.
uncertain_points.risk: If alerts bus carries independent per-alert requests, only bit 0 triggers any sender, leading to missed fault alerts and potential security/functional failures.

uncertain_points.claim: alert_ack_o and alert_state_o are unconnected, ignoring the alert sender's handshake and state; the system may not properly clear or track alerts.
uncertain_points.risk: May cause alert protocol deadlock or inability to detect that an alert was acknowledged, potentially leaving faults unhandled.
